brief: Bonds are panicking while stocks are not reacting. The 10-year yield's RSI is stretched to levels not seen in a long time, comparable to the local yield high in January 2025; Thursday's late move looked like a large position getting stopped out, a warning against chasing yields higher but not a call that the top is in. MOVE has exploded over the past two sessions, meaning bond risk itself, not just the yield level, is being repriced; if the vol spike persists, VaR limits could force bond books to cut risk into the move, adding selling pressure. The MOVE-VIX gap has blown out to extreme levels. SPX has held up against the surge; that divergence can persist if stocks read higher yields as a stronger-growth signal, but gets harder to sustain if bond stress forces broader risk reduction. Jim Reid at Deutsche Bank notes almost all of this year's 10-year yield rise has come from real yields, with little change in inflation expectations, reading it as bonds repricing growth and the rate path rather than an inflation shock. The note's own read: stronger growth may be helping SPX absorb higher yields through earnings, but that is an index-level story, since Russell's weakness shows rate-sensitive stocks are already feeling the squeeze. If real yields stay elevated, the gap between calm equities and panicked bonds becomes harder to ignore.
